newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin promises active return to Kremlin Monday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin promises active return to Kremlin Monday.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, in his first television interview since undergoing heart surgery last month, on Friday told the nation he would return to active work at his Kremlin desk on Monday morning.
"The country needs an active and energetic president, especially now," Yeltsin said, speaking in a firm and decisive voice throughout the interview.
The remarks, recorded by the Kremlin press service, were filmed at the Rus residence outside Moscow where the 65-year-old Russian leader has spent the last stage of his post-operation recovery.
He underwent a multiple heart bypass operation on November 5, and since then has made only brief public remarks.
Dressed in a cardigan and open-neck shirt and sitting in a plush green armchair, the president appeared anxious to tackle the many problems that have mounted during his illness.

"I feel that the recovery period is over. I am returning to the Kremlin on Monday, (December) 23. I will be there at nine a.m. The doctors have done their job and now it is up to the president," he said.
"There is no time for warming up. And also, this is against my character. If I work, I work in earnest," he said.
Yeltsin said the main problems he would have to address were workers' unpaid wages, the peace process in the breakaway region of Chechnya and reform of the army and military doctrine.
"A state that cannot pay its workers for labour they have performed -- this simply cannot be allowed," he said.

Yeltsin has met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and some of his top aides in recent weeks, but has kept only a limited work schedule. His doctors have advised him to not become too engaged in work too quickly after his Kremlin return.
After suffering two heart attacks last year, Yeltsin waged a vigorous campaign for re-election.
He then disappeared from public view shortly before winning a second term on July 3, and in September announced that he would undergo major heart surgery.
Yeltsin is expected to move back into his Moscow home over the weekend.
